message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to compare prices and check compatibility. |
| 2 | **Gather Components** | CPU, motherboard, RAM, storage, GPU, PSU, case, cooling, peripherals. | Stick to a single brand family (e.g., Intel or AMD) for easier compatibility. |
| 3 | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, flat, static‑free surface. | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or work on a grounded mat. |
| 4 | **Install the CPU** | The brain of your system. | 1. Open the CPU socket latch. 2. Align the CPU (triangle marks). 3. Gently place it. 4. Lock the latch. |
| 5 | **Apply Thermal Paste** | Ensures heat transfer from CPU to cooler. | A pea‑size amount in the center is enough. |
| 6 | **Mount the CPU Cooler** | Keeps temperatures low. | Follow the cooler’s manual; use the correct mounting kit for your socket. |
| 7 | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Snap sticks into the correct slots (usually color‑coded). |
| 8 | **Mount the Motherboard** | The backbone connecting everything. | 1. Place standoffs in the case. 2. Align the motherboard with the I/O shield. 3. Secure with screws. |
| 9 | **Install Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Fast boot times and ample space. | 2. SATA SSDs: connect SATA data + power cables. 3. NVMe M.2: slide into the slot and screw down. |
|10 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Delivers power to all components. | 1. Place PSU in the case (bottom or top). 2. Secure with screws. 3. Route cables neatly. |
|11 | **Mount the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | 1. Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers. 2. Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot. 3. Secure with screws. 4. Connect 6‑/8‑pin power cables. |
|12 | **Connect Case Fans & Front Panel** | Power, USB, audio, power button. | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pinouts. |
|13 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | Use zip ties, Velcro straps, or cable combs. |
|14 | **Double‑Check All Connections** | Prevents hardware damage. | Verify that all power connectors are seated and that no cables are pinched. |
|15 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | First boot to confirm everything works. | 1. Turn on the PC. 2. Enter BIOS (usually `Del` or `F2`). 3. Check that CPU, RAM, storage, and GPU are detected. 4. Set boot priority to your OS drive. |
|16 | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Windows, Linux, etc. | Create a bootable USB with the OS installer. Boot from USB, follow prompts. |
|17 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensures hardware runs optimally. | 1. Install motherboard chipset drivers. 2. Install GPU drivers. 3. Run Windows Update or equivalent. |
|18 | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify performance and stability. | Use tools like 3DMark, Cinebench, or Prime95. |
|19 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your PC running smoothly. | Clean dust filters monthly, update firmware, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Component Checklist

| Category | Typical Choices | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|
| **CPU** | Intel Core i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen 5/7/9 | Match socket to motherboard. |
| **Motherboard** | B550 / X570 (AMD), B460 / Z490 (Intel) | Ensure it supports your CPU and has enough PCI‑e slots. |
| **RAM** | 16 GB DDR4 (3200 MHz) | Dual‑channel for best performance. |
| **Storage** | 500 GB NVMe SSD + 1 TB HDD | NVMe for OS, HDD for bulk storage. |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 3060 / AMD RX 6600 XT | Depends on gaming or workstation needs. |
| **PSU** | 650 W 80+ Gold | Sufficient for mid‑range builds. |
| **Case** | Mid‑tower ATX | Good airflow, cable management. |
| **Cooler** | Stock cooler (if included) or aftermarket AIO | For higher‑end CPUs. |

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; double‑check standoffs. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow; use quality thermal paste. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Verify socket, chipset, and power connector specs before buying. |
| **Cable clutter** | Plan cable routes early; use zip ties. |
| **BIOS not detecting GPU** | Make sure GPU is seated fully; check power cables. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & price tracker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and cooler manuals.  

Happy building! If you hit a snag or need component recommendations, just let me know.
